decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display is a low-cost catalog variant of a core format, and with no evidence that its value has failed to materialize, keeping the option open is still worthwhile despite rising paper and energy costs.
The pegboard-back display uses existing cardboard capabilities and costs little to list, so it remains a cheap option even though its distinct demand is still unproven.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a core format with steady retail demand and negligible holding cost, so nothing justifies abandoning it.
The eighth-pallet display completes the format range at minimal marginal cost and serves smaller-footprint promotions, so it stays.

The wooden pallet lies outside the paper core and faces volatile timber costs, but as the firm's only diversification option in a narrow portfolio it is still worth holding unless clear evidence of weak demand emerges.

The media-product display serves a shrinking physical-media niche, which makes abandonment fairly likely, but listing it costs little and the format can be reused for other goods, so it is kept for now.
